items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree, preferably in the fields of social work (BSW), psychology, health care or human services
Experience working in a health care setting.
Experience serving cancer patients and their families.
Experience navigating community resources and linking patients and families to services to assist them.

The role of the Supportive Oncology Patient Navigator is to provide support, education, referrals, and resources to help navigate adult cancer patients throughout their care within the outpatient adult oncology care settings. Under general direction and team collaboration, the Supportive Oncology Patient Navigator conducts needs assessments, identifies barriers to care, coordinates efforts to reduce barriers by connecting patients to UCDH and community services, facilitates logistical needs to improve treatment adherence, and provides education, guidance and support to address supportive care needs.
80% - Patient resource need assessment and coordination
20% - Patient education and care team collaboration
Bilingual fluency – Spanish, Russian, Tagalog or Vietnamese.
Familiarity with oncology knowledge, cancer-related psychosocial impact.
Knowledge of Medicaid/Medi-Cal and educating patients/clients on their benefits and how to use them.
